messages:
Sam: Heads-up — after the merge deployed ~08:30 I have a reproducible p95 spike for short sequences (<64) on first decode after a worker spins up. baseline p95 ~42ms -> observed ~115ms.
Anya: Ugh, which merge? did CI flag anything?
build-bot: perf/throughput-job #523 failed: p95_decode_shortseq +28% vs baseline. https://ci.internal/perf/523
Sam: The deploy included PR#1342 (fused-op-scheduler). merge commit 6b2c9f1.
Dmitri: Can you grab a flame or perf top for a repro run? trying to see if we switched kernels at warmup.
Sam: Pasted perf top from a repro (seq_len=32, batch=1):
```
  38.7%  runtime  attention::matmul_fused_4x4
  19.2%  runtime  scheduler::prefetch_schedule
  12.1%  runtime  kv::hotcopy_path
   7.6%  runtime  fused_dispatch::overhead
```
Kevin: scheduler::prefetch_schedule being large + fused matmul dominating suggests selection picks the fused kernel on cold start and we pay compile/prime + memcopy costs.
Anya: I pulled kernel_selector logs from the failing run: before=matmul_8x8 selected=matmul_fused_4x4 at seq<=64, decision time 12:02:15. That decision correlates with the PR change.
Sam: Instrumented trace shows the slow path is only on the very first decode after model instance creation. token0 ~72ms in kernel prime+kv copy; token1+ ~9ms. So transient but hurts p95 for short-lived sessions.
Dmitri: Sounds like the selection score is optimizing steady-state throughput and omitting a warmup penalty (prime + prefetch). We should repro locally with debug flags.
Sam: Repro steps I ran:
```
RUN_MODEL --model rdx-small --seq 32 --batch 1 --skip-warmup
# run 2000 single-request inferences, measure p95
```
Kevin: I bisected 6b2c9f1..2ad3f8e (last-green 2ad3f8e). Culprit narrowed to scheduler::choose_prefetch_strategy() change in PR#1342.
Anya: PR notes say it prefers fused matmul on small sequences to lower steady-state latency. but it didn't account for "first request" cost: kernel prime + KV prefetch copy.
Sam: Timeline from profiler: first token spends ~70-80ms doing kernel-init + memcopy, subsequent tokens ~7-10ms. Short sessions see the first-token penalized at p95.
Kevin: Options: revert PR#1342; add instance_age-aware penalty to kernel scoring; or force a cheaper kernel for the first N tokens. Revert is heavy, but safest.
Anya: I prefer a targeted change: add a warmup_penalty to kernel scores when instance_age < X ms. Also add telemetry of selection decisions so we can verify in canary. Hold the rollout until we validate.
Dmitri: Also let's add a microbenchmark that simulates cold-start single requests to the perf suite. CI currently measures steady-state only.
build-bot: PERF-REQ-712 opened to add cold-start microbench to perf CI.
Sam: I'll open a patch to kernel_selector that subtracts a warmup penalty equivalent (e.g., add +30ms to fused kernel score if instance_age < 500ms). will run local benches and open PR.
Kevin: Run with my quick bench on your patch (PR#1360) — lokal run shows p95 back to ~46ms (baseline 42ms) and no perf failure in a few runs. Good signal but need CI.
Anya: Thanks — add verbose selection logs (chosen kernel, score components, instance_age) so we can audit decisions post-merge. I'll freeze the canary rollout until perf CI picks up the microbench and green.
eng-oncall-bot: Canary freeze active. Notifying eng-oncall channel. Pager suppressed.
Dmitri: Once PR#1360 lands I'll rerun the bisect-run and smoke tests against the worst-case workload. If the p95 doesn't return to baseline, we revert.
Sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/rdx/pull/1360 — kernel_selector: incorporate instance_age warmup_penalty. Bench results included in description.
Kevin: Verified locally against a clean checkout + PR1360 branch: p95 ~47ms, steady-state unchanged.
Anya: Great. After CI picks up PERF-REQ-712 and green, we'll unfreeze canary and roll the change. Please add a short postmortem note summarizing root cause and the guardrail (cold-start microbench + logs).
Sam: Will do a brief postmortem and add the microbenchmark to the perf suite. Follow-ups: (1) telemetry for selection decisions, (2) cold-start perf CI, (3) consider making kernel_selector tests part of PR checks. Thanks everyone.
